subject: How to export original multilocus genotypes dataset outside Poppr/R

messages.author: 8ce694d5545e48a5
messages.subject: How to export original multilocus genotypes dataset outside Poppr/R
parts:
Hello,

Could you please help me to find the way to export dataset of original multilocus genotypes into Excel or other document from R? Here is the information about my genclone object:

Genotype information:

   517 original multilocus genotypes 
   759 haploid individuals
     7 codominant loci

Population information:

     1 stratum - Pop
     6 populations defined - Blackb, Blueb, Currant, Grape, Raspb, Strawb


I need to get a datasheet/table of 517 original multilocus genotypes (the dataset that does not contain clones) that I could use outside R. I got to the point where I was able to filter them with the command mlg.filter(popsc) <- .Machine$double.eps, and I got the following:

Genotype information:

   517 contracted multilocus genotypes
       (0) [t], (diss.dist) [d], (farthest) [a] 
   759 haploid individuals
     7 codominant loci


Now I need to export these 517 contracted multilocus genotypes into the file (csv or excel), however cannot find the way to do so yet.

I will be very grateful for help and suggestions.

Thank you

Olga

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to export original multilocus genotypes dataset outside Poppr/R
parts:
Hello Olga,

To reduce your data set to the number of unique genotypes, you can use the function clonecorrect(). By default, it will retain unique genotypes within each population, but keep duplicated genotypes across populations, but you can change that by setting strata = NA 

After you clone correct your data set, you can export it to a data frame with genind2df() and then write it to a table using any number of functions from R. I recommend using write_csv() from the "readr" package. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian

-----

Department of Plant Pathology
